title: Effects of gender and personality on experience of small living spaces: Ceiling height and floor plan shape in virtual environment

findings.antecedent: Floor plan shape (long, rectangular vs. short, square-like)
findings.mechanism: A space with a more square-like floor plan provided a more open look, leading to greater connection.
findings.quote: floor plan shape showed a significant impact on the mean of place attachment (β = -0.165, t (45.1) = -3.38, p = 0.0009)
Whereas ceiling height was not a significant predictor of mean place attachment

findings.antecedent: Floor plan shape x Ceiling height interaction

findings.quote: participants rated higher functional or goal-oriented connections to high ceiling spaces than to low ceiling spaces.

findings.mechanism: A space with a more square-like floor plan provided a more open look.
findings.quote: floor plan shape has a negative impact on place identity (β = −0.67, t (133.3) = -5.79, p = 0.01).

findings.mechanism: A space with a more square-like floor plan provided a more open look.
findings.quote: a significant negative floor plan shape effect on place dependence was found (β = −0.62, t (131.3) = 1.15, p < 0.05).

findings.mechanism: Participants had more affective bonding to a square space than a long rectangular space.
findings.quote: Floor plan shape had a strong negative impact on personal sense of place (β = -0.91, t (131.3) = -0.74, p = 0.0003)

findings.mechanism: Participants reported a lower partial sense of place after viewing the long floor plans than they did after viewing short floor plans.
findings.quote: floor plan shape showed a negative impact on the partial sense of place (β = 0.62, t (131.3) = -1.42, p < 0.05).

findings.mechanism: More extroverted participants rated lower place attachment regardless of spatial design elements.
findings.quote: Extroversion was found to have a significant negative impact on place attachment (β = -0.59, t (6) = −2.66, p = 0.0086).
extroversion had a negative impact on place identity (β = -0.86, t (6) = −3.7, p = 0.0003)

findings.mechanism: More extrovert participants felt significantly more functional connections to high ceiling spaces than low ceiling spaces.

findings.quote: Men reported significantly more affective ties with longer floor plans than with the short floor plan (β = 0.18, t (41.0) = 0.76, p = 0.001).

findings.quote: The older age group thought that the spaces with long floor plan shape, which is rectangular in shape, were more functional than the shorter ones (Table 9).

findings.antecedent: Extroversion score (higher) x Floor plan shape (longer floor plans)

findings.quote: more extroverted people reported a higher personal sense of place after viewing the rectangular spaces than they did with the square spaces (Table 10).

findings.antecedent: Age (older group) x Floor plan shape (longer floor plans)
findings.mechanism: Older age group reported a lower partial sense of place after viewing the long floor plans than they did after viewing the short floor plans.

stimuli.description: Four 3D virtual mock-ups of small living spaces (236 sq ft) shown as walkthrough videos. Conditions varied by ceiling height (low: 7'6" vs. high: 9'6") and floor plan shape (short/square-like: 15'4"x15'4" vs. long/rectangular: 10'x23'6"). All spaces included a bathroom, kitchen, and bedroom/living room area with identical interior elements.

limitations: The scope can be extended to include other design elements, such as furniture and windows, and additional user traits.

Advanced immersive virtual environments utilizing VR and augmented reality technologies offer lifelike experiences so that researchers will not have to question their reliability. As the technology becomes more sophisticated, more researchers for spatial user experience studies should consider the opportunities to tackle problems that were not accessible otherwise.
